subject: Big Poe #07
text: Big Poe #07 appears at the intersection of the three-way road near Gerudo Valley when approached from the south while facing towards the gap.

evidence.quote: ------------ Big Poe #07 Location: The intersection of the three-way road near Gerudo Valley.

subject: Big Poe #08
text: Big Poe #08 appears when riding north from the road near Gerudo Valley and passing by the west side of the lone tree west of Lon Lon Ranch.

evidence.quote: ------------ Big Poe #08 Location: The lone tree west of Lon Lon Ranch.

subject: Big Poe #08
text: Follow Big Poe #08 to the top of the hill and shoot it when the hill levels out rather than trying to shoot it uphill.

evidence.quote: Big Poe #08 ... The only disadvantage to this one is the Poe will be going uphill, making this an extremely difficult shot.  Your best bet is to not even try to shoot it when it first appears, but just follow it to the top of the hill, and then shoot it when the hill levels out further up.

subject: Big Poe #09
text: Big Poe #09 appears near bushes south of the river in northwest Hyrule Field when riding southeast from the corner where the wall and river meet towards the Lon Lon Ranch tree.

evidence.quote: ------------ Big Poe #09 Location: South of the river in northwest Hyrule Field.

subject: Big Poe #10
text: Big Poe #10 appears near the lone tree outside Lon Lon Ranch when brushing along the southern edge of the tree while riding west.

evidence.quote: ------------ Big Poe #10 Location: The lone tree near the entrance to Lon Lon Ranch.

subject: Empty Bottle
text: Killing Big Poe #10 and returning all ten Big Poes to the Poe Shop earns an Empty Bottle.

evidence.quote: Big Poe #10 ... Kill it and take it back to the Poe Shop, and you'll have earned your Bottle.

subject: Deku Stick
text: Young Link can use Deku Sticks to transfer fire from a lit torch to adjacent unlit torches around a room, though the stick expires if lit for too long.

evidence.quote: Deku Sticks are tools commonly used by Young Link.  With them, Young Link can light the Sticks on a lit torch, and transfer that flame to adjacent torches around the room.  The Stick expires if lit for too long.

subject: Deku Baba
text: Deku Babas drop Deku Sticks if Link stuns them and kills them while their stem extends straight into the air.

evidence.quote: Deku Sticks are commonly found on Deku Babas; to obtain them from the enemies, stun them and then kill them while their stem extends straight in the air.

subject: Deku Nut
text: Deku Nuts explode in a bright flash upon striking the ground to stun vulnerable enemies and destroy Shabom bubbles in Jabu-Jabu's Belly, but have no effect on minibosses and bosses.

evidence.quote: An item used exclusively in combat, Deku Nuts explode in a bright flash when they strike the ground.  The flash temporarily stuns all enemies in the area who are vulnerable to the stun.  Deku Nuts are particularly effective against the bubble-like Shabom enemies in Jabu-Jabu's Belly, as the bubbles are destroyed by the Nut's flash.  Deku Nuts have absolutely no effect on more powerful enemies, i.e. Minibosses and Bosses.

subject: Fairy Slingshot
text: The Fairy Slingshot is the first ranged weapon found in Inside the Deku Tree for Young Link and is effectively replaced by the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: First Found: Inside the Deku Tree...The first ranged weapon in the game, the Fairy Slingshot is also the weakest ranged weapon in the game.  It is one of the items used most regularly by Young Link, but it is effectively replaced by the more powerful Boomerang, which also has the bonus of having infinite ammo.

subject: Fairy Ocarina
text: Saria gives Young Link the Fairy Ocarina in Kokiri Forest, which is used most frequently to open doorways with Zelda's Lullaby until obtaining the Ocarina of Time.

evidence.quote: First Found: Kokiri Forest...A gift from Link's Kokiri friend, Saria, the Fairy Ocarina is essentially a placeholder for Young Link until he obtains the Ocarina of Time after the third dungeon.  The Fairy Ocarina is used most frequently to open doorways using Zelda's Lullaby, but can be used to play other songs.

subject: Bottles
text: Bottles can store restorative items like Fairies and Lon Lon Milk, as well as capture Bugs and Blue Fire.

evidence.quote: Bottles, long a staple of the Zelda series, are used to store helpful restorative items like Fairies and Lon Lon Milk.  Bottles can also be used to capture Bugs and Blue Fire, which have their own uses in the game.

subject: Empty Bottle
text: Young Link obtains the first of four Empty Bottles from Talon at Lon Lon Ranch after finding all three Special Cuccos among the flock of Normal Cuccos.

evidence.quote: The first bottle in the game is obtained with Young Link, and is won from Talon in Lon Lon Ranch after you have awoken him in the Hyrule Castle Garden.  Find all three of his "Special Cuccos" in the flock of Normal Cuccos, and he'll award you with an Empty Bottle, the first of four.

subject: Empty Bottle
text: Young Link obtains the second bottle in Kakariko Village by gathering all the Cuccos in town and returning them to the Cucco Pasture near the graveyard entrance.

evidence.quote: The second bottle in the game is also obtained by Young Link.  In Kakariko Village, gather all of the Cuccos in town and return them to the Cucco Pasture near the entrance to Kakariko Graveyard.  Three of the Cuccos can only be reached by gliding off of cliffs and over fences using other Cuccos.

subject: Empty Bottle
text: Young Link retrieves the third bottle from the bottom of Lake Hylia by diving down after obtaining the Silver Scale.

evidence.quote: The third bottle in the game is, again, obtained by Young Link, and is also the only Bottle that you HAVE to get.  Once you have earned the Silver Scale, head for Lake Hylia and dive down to retrieve the Bottle from the Lake's bottom.

subject: Empty Bottle
text: Adult Link receives the fourth bottle from the Poe Man in Hyrule Castle after capturing all ten Big Poes in Hyrule Field using Epona and the Fairy Bow.

evidence.quote: The last bottle in the game is the only one found by Adult Link.  Once you have Epona and the Fairy Bow, hunt down and capture all ten of the Big Poes in Hyrule Field and deliver them to the Poe Shop in Hyrule Castle.  The Poe Man will give you the fourth bottle when you do.

subject: Bombs
text: Bombs are stored in a pouch made from a Dodongo's Stomach, are first found as the dungeon item in Dodongo's Cavern, and are used to blow open weakened walls and defeat King Dodongo.

evidence.quote: First Found: Dodongo's Cavern...The "Goron's Special Crop" is stored in a special pouch made from a Dodongo's Stomach.  Bombs can be used to blow open weakened walls, and are required to defeat certain armored enemies and solve a number of other minor puzzles.  They are also instrumental in defeating the King Dodongo.  The Bombs are first found as the dungeon item in Dodongo's Cavern.

subject: Bombchus
text: Bombchus are mobile bombs that climb walls and explode on contact, and they can be bought from the shop in the Back Alley or won from the Bombchu Bowling Alley after Dodongo's Cavern.

evidence.quote: Bombchus are mobile bombs which follow a straight line and then explode when they contact something.  They have the ability to climb along walls, and to a lesser extent ceilings.  The earliest time that you can obtain them is in the Hyrule Castle Market, immediately after finishing Dodongo's Cavern.  You can either buy them from the shop in the Back Alley, or win them from the Bombchu Bowling Alley.

subject: Din's Fire
text: Din's Fire creates an expanding ring of fire that burns enemies and lights torches, and it is obtained at the dead end in Hyrule Castle Garden immediately after getting Bombs from Dodongo's Cavern.

evidence.quote: First Found: Hyrule Castle Garden...When used, this spell creates a ring of fire that expands out and encompasses everything in the room.  It will burn any enemies it makes contact with, and also lights any unlit torches it makes contact with.  Din's Fire is used primarily to solve several torch-lighting puzzles throughout the game, but is also useful against several smaller, weakened enemies, such as the Mini-Floor Masters.  Din's Fire can be obtained from the dead end in Hyrule Castle Garden immediately after obtaining the Bombs from Dodongo's Cavern.

subject: Magic Beans
text: Magic Beans planted in soft earth as Young Link grow into flying Magic Leaves that Adult Link can ride to reach out-of-reach areas.

evidence.quote: The Magic Beans can be planted in the plots of soft earth that dot the Hyrule countryside as Young Link.  Once planted, these beans begin to grow, and when you return to these areas with Adult Link, you will find a flying Magic Leaf that can be used to access out-of-reach areas.

subject: Magic Beans
text: The Bean Man upstream in Zora's River sells 10 Magic Beans starting at 10 Rupees, with each successive bean increasing by 10 Rupees up to 100 Rupees, for a grand total of 550 Rupees.

evidence.quote: The Magic Beans are purchased from the Bean Man upstream from the entrance to Zora's River.  He has ten total to sell.  The Magic Beans cost 10 Rupees initially, but raise in price by 10 rupees for each successive purchased Bean, until the final Bean reaches 100 rupees.  All 10 Beans cost a grand total of 550 rupees.
